 In The Court Of Ms. Samiksha Gupta
 Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate
 South West District; Dwarka Courts: New Delhi
Date of Institution : 22.10.2021
Date of Reserving Judgment : 12.09.2024
Date of Judgment : 21.09.2024
In the matter of :
State Vs. Pranya Bhatia
Fir No. 79/2021
Ps : Sector-23 Dwarka
U/s: 75 Juvenile Justice (Care &
Protection of Children) Act, 2015
1. Registration. No. of Case : 13228/2021
2. Cnr No. of Case : Dlsw02-050583-2021
3. Name of complainant : Raj Bhatia
 S/o Late Sh. S. P. Bhatia,
 R/o B-313, 2nd Floor, Hari Nagar,
 New Delhi-110064. 
4. Name of accused : Pranya Bhatia  W/o Sh. Raj Bhatia  R/o Vivanta Apartment sec 23,
 Dwarka, Sector 23, Dwarka,
 New Delhi.
5. Offence charged under : 75, Juvenile Justice (Care &
 Section Protection of Children) Act, 2015 State Vs. Pranya Bhatia FIR 79/2021, PS Sector-23 Dwarka Page No.1 of 11  6. Plea of accused : Not guilty 7. Final Order : Acquitted State represented by : Sh. Rohit Grewal, APP for State.
Accused represented by : Sh. Neeraj Jakhar and Sh. Jitender Sapra,
 Advocates. 
State vs Pranya Bhatiya on 21 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162029839/
1 Complainant represented by: Sh. Harish Sharma and Ms. Poonam  Sharma, Advocates  JUDGMENT 1. It is the case of prosecution that on and before 09.03.2021 at flat No. A-14, Shaman Vihar Apartment, Sector 23 Dwarka, accused scolded and beat up her daughters, Yashika and Yashvi. Due to such behaviour, she caused them unnecessary mental and physical suffering. Thus, prosecution has set up a case under Section 75 Juvenile Justice Act ("JJ Act", hereinafter) against accused Pranya Bhatia. 
2. On the basis of investigation carried out by police, charge sheet was filed in Court and copy of the same was supplied to accused. 
3. On the basis of charge sheet, charge for committing offences punishable under Section 75 JJ Act was framed against accused to which she pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 
State Vs. Pranya Bhatia FIR 79/2021, PS Sector-23 Dwarka Page No.2 of 11 4. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined four witnesses, who are as under:
Sr. Name Nature of Evidence No 1. PW-1/'Y' Child victim 2. PW-2/'Y' Child victim 3. PW-3/Raj Bhatia Complainant 4. PW-4/SI Sandeep Singh IO 5. Prosecution has relied upon the following documents:
S. Exhibits Documents No.
1. Ex.PW-1/A Statement of child victim 2. Ex.A3 Statement under Section 164 Cr.PC of PW-1 3. Ex.PW-4/D Statement of PW1 under Section 161 Cr.PC  Mark X1 4. Ex.A2 Statement u/s 164 Cr.PC of PW2 5. Ex.A-1 (colly) FIR 6 . Ex.PW-4/A Ruqqa 7. Ex.PW-4/B Application for recording statement under Section 164  Cr.PC 8. Mark X3 Letter dated 30.11.2020 9. Ex.PW-4/C Notice under Section 41-A Cr.PC State vs Pranya Bhatiya on 21 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162029839/
2 6. Thereafter, PE was closed and statement of accused was recorded wherein she stated that false case has been filed against her. She did not lead any evidence in defence. 
State Vs. Pranya Bhatia FIR 79/2021, PS Sector-23 Dwarka Page No.3 of 11 7. Arguments heard. Record perused. 
8. To prove the charge under Section 75 JJ Act, the prosecution is required to prove beyond reasonable doubt, the following components:-
a) Accused must have actual charge of or control over the child victim; and b) Accused must have assaulted, abandoned, abused or willfully neglected the child victim; or c) Accused must have caused in some manner to have assaulted, abandoned, abused or willfully neglected the child victim; and d) Such act of accused must have caused or likely to have caused unnecessary mental or physical suffering to the child victim.
9. The evidence of prosecution witnesses in the present case has to be examined against this legal position. 
(i) Child victim/PW-1 Ms. 'Y' was one of the victims in the present case. Certain questions were put to the child witness and after preliminary inquiry, her testimony was recorded in Court. 
During her evidence, she stated that complaint against her mother was given by her at the instance of her father. She further deposed that no incident of misbehaviour or abuse by any other person had occurred with her. 
State Vs. Pranya Bhatia FIR 79/2021, PS Sector-23 Dwarka Page No.4 of 11 She was cross examined by Ld. APP for State as she had resiled from her previous statement. She stated that she was residing with her father in March 2021. She denied the suggestion that her mother used to physically and mentally torture her and younger sister regularly on minor issues. She further stated that her mother used to scold them when they did not study. She denied the suggestion that her mother had beaten her with danda. She admitted that her statement was recorded before Ld. MM and that she had signed the complaint Ex.PW-1/A after reading the same. She denied the suggestion that her mother beat her with a sugarcane. She denied the suggestion that accused/mother did not let them meet their father. She denied the suggestion that her mother and one Tarun used to have obscene chats. She denied the suggestion that she was deposing falsely since her custody presently was with her mother/accused. 
State vs Pranya Bhatiya on 21 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162029839/
3 She was not cross examined despite opportunity by accused. 
(ii) Child victim/PW-2 Ms. 'Y' was one of the victims in the present case. Certain questions were put to the child witness and after preliminary inquiry, her testimony was recorded in Court. 
During her evidence, she stated that complaint against her mother was given by her at the instance of her father. She further deposed that no incident of misbehaviour or abuse by any other person had occurred with her. 
She was cross examined by Ld. APP for State as she had resiled from her previous statement. She stated that she was residing with her father in March 2021. She denied the suggestion that her mother gave State Vs. Pranya Bhatia FIR 79/2021, PS Sector-23 Dwarka Page No.5 of 11 beatings to her sister PW1 with danda. She denied the suggestion that her mother used to scold her and her sister and abused them in filthy language. She admitted that her statement was recorded before Ld.
MM. She denied the suggestion that she was deposing falsely since her custody presently was with her mother/accused. 
She was not cross examined despite opportunity by accused. 
(iii) PW-3 Raj Bhatia deposed that accused was his wife and till 2020, they were on cordial terms. In November, 2020, he found one letter written by his elder daughter Yashvi in the drawer of the mandir. Upon reading the said letter, he found that his wife used to torture and beat their daughters and that she had an extra martial affair with one Tarun Ranjan. In December 2020, he found one more letter written by her daughters. Upon reading, he found out that his wife used to take their daughters to one tantrik and used to do objectionable things. His daughters also told him that accused used to get angry on petty matters and used to threaten them with knife. One day, she also hit their elder daughter with sugarcane on her thigh. Further, accused did not care that their daughters were not given proper food in daycare. Witness also stated that their daughters had told him that accused used to put some tantrik ash in their food. Since he was scared about the safety of their children, he left the house along with them. He took their daughters to PS and the present case was registered against accused. 
During cross-examination, he denied the suggestion that both the daughters were under his influence, being in his custody, and therefore, State Vs. Pranya Bhatia FIR 79/2021, PS Sector-23 Dwarka Page No.6 of 11 they had given false statement to the police. He denied the suggestion that accused never used any abusive language or gave beatings to their children. 
(iv) PW-4 SI Sandeep deposed that upon statement of child victim on 09.03.2021, ruqqa was prepared and present FIR was got registered. After registration of FIR, statements of both victims were recorded. Their statements under Section 164 Cr.PC were also recorded. Counselling of both the victims were got done before CWC. Copy of letter was provided by the father/PW-3. Further investigation was conducted and charge sheet was filed. He correctly identified the accused present in Court. 
State vs Pranya Bhatiya on 21 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162029839/
4 During cross-examination, he denied the suggestion that statements of child victims was recorded under duress. He denied the suggestion that charge sheet was filed without proper investigation. 
10. Analysis & Findings:
(i) Perusal of record shows that one complaint under Section 156 (3) Cr.PC was initially filed by the father of child victims, Raj Bhatia against accused. The present FIR, however, was registered on the basis of complaint by one child victim. Perusal of said complaint and chargesheet shows that there are allegations of cruelty, abuse and wanton neglect on the part of accused towards her minor daughters. 
(ii) As per prosecution version, accused used to physically and State Vs. Pranya Bhatia FIR 79/2021, PS Sector-23 Dwarka Page No.7 of 11 mentally torture her two minor daughters. She also used to beat and abuse them on minor issues. 
Per contra, it is the version of accused that she has been falsely implicated at the instance of her husband (father of victims) to settle scores due to marital discord between them. It was further contended on her behalf that her minor daughters were manipulated by their father (husband of accused) and that they were tutored by him and present case was filed against her on such false and concocted facts. 
(iii) The prosecution is required to prove beyond reasonable doubt that :
(a) Both minor daughters/child victim were in the custody or actual charge of accused; and (b) Accused person knowingly assaulted/willfully neglected them by her acts which caused unnecessary mental/physical suffering to them.
(iv) In the present case, the evidence of prosecution rests on the testimony of child victims/minor daughters who were examined as PW1 and PW2. However, during their evidence recorded in Court, they resiled from their previous statements in material particulars and were cross examined by Ld. APP. 
(v) During their evidence, both child victims stated that the State Vs. Pranya Bhatia FIR 79/2021, PS Sector-23 Dwarka Page No.8 of 11 complaint against their mother/accused was given by them at the instance of their father. They also categorically denied any incident of misbehavior towards them by the accused. 
(vi) During their cross examination by Ld. APP, they denied that accused used to physically assault or mentally torture them on minor issues. They in fact stated that accused scolded them only when they did not study. They categorically denied that accused used to beat them with a stick or sugarcane, as alleged. 
State vs Pranya Bhatiya on 21 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162029839/
5 (vii) They also stated that they were staying with their father in March 2021 after accused left the house on 05.01.2021. It is pertinent to state that the present FIR was registered on 09.03.2021. Further, the father of child victims/PW3 came to know about such cruel acts of accused by way of a letter which was written by his daughters/child victims. The said letter has not been proved as per law. The original letter was never produced in Court or seized by IO. 
(viii) It is also pertinent to state that both the victims were child victims. It has been contended on behalf of complainant that child victims have resiled from their statements due to fear of accused which shows the conduct of accused. 
Similarly, accused has contended that complaint against her was filed by her daughters at the time when they were in their father's custody and allegations were made at his behest. 
State Vs. Pranya Bhatia FIR 79/2021, PS Sector-23 Dwarka Page No.9 of 11 (ix) The evidence of child witnesses has to be evaluated with caution. The age of child witnesses at the time of evidence was 14 and 11 years. At the time of registration of FIR, their age was 11 and 8 years. 
(x) The Indian Evidence Act, 1872 does not prescribe any particular age as a determinative factor to treat a witness to be a competent one. On the contrary, Section 118 of Evidence Act envisages that all persons shall be competent to testify, unless the court considers that they are prevented from understanding the questions put to them or from giving rational answers to these questions, because of tender years, extreme old age, disease whether of mind, or any other cause of the same kind. 
(xi) The evidence of a child witness is not required to be rejected per se, but the court as a rule of prudence considers such evidence with close scrutiny and only on being convinced about the quality thereof and reliability can record conviction, based thereon. Reliance in this regard is placed on judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Suryanarayana v. State of Karnataka (2001 (9) SCC 129). 
It was further observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Dattu Ramrao Sakhare v. State of Maharashtra (1997) 5 SCC 341 that:
"A child witness if found competent to depose to the facts and reliable one such evidence could be the basis of conviction. In other words even in the absence of oath the evidence of a child witness can be considered under Section 118 of the Evidence Act provided that such witness is able to understand the questions State Vs. Pranya Bhatia FIR 79/2021, PS Sector-23 Dwarka Page No.10 of 11 and able to give rational answers thereof. The evidence of a child witness and credibility thereof would depend upon the circumstances of each case. The only precaution which the court should bear in mind while assessing the evidence of a child witness is that the witness must be a reliable one and his/her demeanour must be like any other competent witness and there is no likelihood of being tutored."
State vs Pranya Bhatiya on 21 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162029839/
6 Thus, as a rule of prudence and precaution, the prosecution was required to corroborate the version of child victims. However, the letter which forms the basis of prosecution case has not been produced in evidence. Further, the testimony of child witnesses in which they have completely resiled from their previous versions cannot be relied on to prove the allegations against accused. In such a scenario, the accused herein is entitled to benefit of doubt. 
11. Accordingly, the prosecution has not been able to prove the guilt of accused in respect of offence u/s 75 JJ Act beyond reasonable doubt. In view of the above discussion, accused Pranya Bhatia is acquitted in the present case. Digitally signed by Samiksha Gupta Samiksha Pronounced in open Court Gupta Date:

8. To prove the charge under Section 75 JJ Act, the prosecution is required to prove beyond reasonable doubt, the following components:-
a) Accused must have actual charge of or control over the child victim; and b) Accused must have assaulted, abandoned, abused or willfully neglected the child victim; or c) Accused must have caused in some manner to have assaulted, abandoned, abused or willfully neglected the child victim; and d) Such act of accused must have caused or likely to have caused unnecessary mental or physical suffering to the child victim.
9. The evidence of prosecution witnesses in the present case has to be examined against this legal position.

(iii) The prosecution is required to prove beyond reasonable doubt that :
(a) Both minor daughters/child victim were in the custody or actual charge of accused; and (b) Accused person knowingly assaulted/willfully neglected them by her acts which caused unnecessary mental/physical suffering to them.
(iv) In the present case, the evidence of prosecution rests on the testimony of child victims/minor daughters who were examined as PW1 and PW2.
However, during their evidence recorded in Court, they resiled from their previous statements in material particulars and were cross examined by Ld. APP.
summary.arguments:
It has been contended on behalf of complainant that child victims have resiled from their statements due to fear of accused which shows the conduct of accused.

Similarly, accused has contended that complaint against her was filed by her daughters at the time when they were in their father's custody and allegations were made at his behest.
summary.ANALYSIS:
State Vs. Pranya Bhatia FIR 79/2021, PS Sector-23 Dwarka Page No.9 of 11 (ix) The evidence of child witnesses has to be evaluated with caution.
The age of child witnesses at the time of evidence was 14 and 11 years.
At the time of registration of FIR, their age was 11 and 8 years.

(x) The Indian Evidence Act, 1872 does not prescribe any particular age as a determinative factor to treat a witness to be a competent one.
On the contrary, Section 118 of Evidence Act envisages that all persons shall be competent to testify, unless the court considers that they are prevented from understanding the questions put to them or from giving rational answers to these questions, because of tender years, extreme old age, disease whether of mind, or any other cause of the same kind.

(xi) The evidence of a child witness is not required to be rejected per se, but the court as a rule of prudence considers such evidence with close scrutiny and only on being convinced about the quality thereof and reliability can record conviction, based thereon.
Reliance in this regard is placed on judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Suryanarayana v. State of Karnataka (2001 (9) SCC 129).

It was further observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Dattu Ramrao Sakhare v. State of Maharashtra (1997) 5 SCC 341 that:
"A child witness if found competent to depose to the facts and reliable one such evidence could be the basis of conviction.
Thus, as a rule of prudence and precaution, the prosecution was required to corroborate the version of child victims.
However, the letter which forms the basis of prosecution case has not been produced in evidence.
Further, the testimony of child witnesses in which they have completely resiled from their previous versions cannot be relied on to prove the allegations against accused.
In such a scenario, the accused herein is entitled to benefit of doubt.
11. Accordingly, the prosecution has not been able to prove the guilt of accused in respect of offence u/s 75 JJ Act beyond reasonable doubt.
